activities.anchor: Treat the statistics office as a witness to be interviewed, not an oracle
activities.caption: file the four doors — how does this data arrive?
activities.name: djDoorsBuckets

config.prompt: Data has four great doors. File each acquisition:

items.label: national statistics offices and spending dashboards
a CSV compelled from a public body, with internal-review appeals
code extracting data from public-access web pages
the Panama Papers: 11.6 million documents across 76 countries

config.why: A well-drafted FOIA request is often itself the scoop — and most big FOIA stories were refused at least once before the appeal ladder produced them.

activities.anchor: if your £41.2 million disagrees with their £43.0 million
activities.caption: rebuild the cleaning checklist, step by step
activities.name: djCleanOrder

config.prompt: A council-spending file, 12,000 rows. Order the cleaning steps:
items: Standardise supplier names and collapse the variants — 12,000 rows become 11,847 unique payments
Replace '-999' amounts with nulls and exclude them from sums
Parse all dates to ISO, drop the embedded totals rows
Recompute the grand total and reconcile against the published annual figure
If your £41.2m disagrees with their £43.0m, the gap is the next FOIA request
config.why: Cleaning is where the hours actually go — and every anomaly fixed is a question about the institution that produced the file.

activities.caption: pair the dataset question with what it exposes
activities.name: djInterviewMatch

config.prompt: The dataset gets the interview a human source would get:

pairs.right: an underfunded inspectorate logs fewer violations
records look complete the year new software arrived — an IT project, not medicine
waiting time from referral differs from from-diagnosis; redefinitions manufacture trends
cross-check totals against an independent published figure

config.why: The answers become the caveats paragraph of the story — the reader's defence is the analysis's honesty about itself.

activities.caption: bet first — the disguised missing value
activities.name: djMissingPredict

config.q: A headline: 'Hospital deaths up 20%.' What must you check before the number becomes a story?
choices: Deaths genuinely rose — the official figure is checked already
Whether case numbers rose 20% too — always convert counts to rates before comparing
Nothing: a 20% rise is large enough to speak for itself
config.why: Denominators: 'hospital deaths up 20%' may mean case numbers rose 20% — always convert counts to rates (per capita, per patient, per vehicle-mile) before comparing.

activities.anchor: asking precisely — specify the date range
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the FOIA request
activities.name: djFoiaSpot

config.prompt: One line of this FOIA request draft is wrong — click it:
lines: Request: all food-hygiene inspection records for the past three years.
Specify the date range: January 2022 to December 2024.
Specify the fields and disaggregation: by month, by postcode district.
Specify the format: a PDF scan of the printed register is acceptable.
config.correction: Ask for a CSV, not a PDF scan — a well-drafted request specifies date range, fields, format and disaggregation.
config.why: A vague request earns a vague answer; the format clause is what makes the release analysable instead of re-typable only by hand.

activities.caption: call the magnitude — the row-count illusion
activities.name: djRowEstimate

config.prompt: The claim: 'burglary doubled in the city centre last year.' The sceptic's pass finds a doubling from 6 to 12 incidents. How many extra burglaries is that?
config.why: Six extra burglaries — well inside ordinary year-to-year noise. Small numbers carry wide confidence, and often the honest story is 'the counting changed'.
config.context: Before the number: check the denominator and the geography, the counting unit, and the series for a structural break at the date of a policy or software change.
